read: 2026-09-29 (the five 1988 worlds) and 2026-10-03 (the five hidden worlds)
how: Every drawable position in the five shipped worlds, read off the 1988 tile as a character grid and at 6x beside the served VIP tile. "pose" is what the original shows; "vip" is the verdict on the tile the VIP build served that day. Rows and columns count the 16x16 tile from 0 at the top left. The five hidden worlds were read on 3 October 2026 off Aleksi Sahala's sheets the same way, with no served VIP tile to judge, so their entries carry no "vip" verdict. They describe HIS drawing, not the 1988 game.

Mid-stride, legs well apart: front foot forward at screen-left, back foot behind at screen-right, both on the ground. Both arms swing out - front hand forward at screen-left, back hand behind at screen-right, at waist height.

pattern.hunter: Walks: each side pair is stride (0, 4) then legs-together passing step (1, 5); the up and down pairs are mirror images, alternating which foot is planted and which hand is raised. Arm-out pairs: 8 and 11 are feet-together leaning pushes, 9 and 10 braced strides. Idle A is a fidget facing the viewer (still, hand on hip with foot tap, mouth open, head turned right with hands on hips); idle B is a hopping spin - crouch facing right, jump facing the viewer, crouch facing left, jump seen from behind.
pattern.cook: Side walks alternate a wide stride with arms in (0, 4) and feet together with both arms flung out (1, 5); up and down pairs alternate the planted foot. Arm-out pairs: 8 and 10 feet together, 9 and 11 a short step. Idle A is only two pictures (12=14, 13=15): lift the screen-right knee with eyes open, then put it down and blink. Idle B keeps the feet planted and rubs his tummy in a circle (belly right, chest high with a laughing grin, chest left, belly low with head bowed).
pattern.cowboy: Side walks are legs together FIRST (0, 4) then stride (1, 5) - the reverse of hunter. Up and down pairs alternate which boot is lifted one pixel. Arm-out pairs: 8 and 11 braced legs-apart lunges reaching the tile edge, 9 and 10 legs together drawn back. Idle A marks time facing the viewer: screen-left boot up, both down with eyes closed, screen-right boot up, both down eyes open. Idle B hops round: front standing, front hopping, back standing, back hopping.
pattern.space: Side walks alternate a stride with the gloves at the hips (96/32) and a legs-together passing step with both arms swung wide front and back (112/48). Up and down walks alternate which foot is lifted, the arm on the same side swinging out. Arm-out pairs keep the feet together throughout and differ only by the arm reaching one pixel further. Idle A is arms straight out to the sides with a toe tap of the screen-right foot (192=224 foot up, 208=240 both down). Idle B turns the head screen-left, front, screen-right, front, with the arms spread down and out, lifted in a shrug, spread, then hanging.
pattern.body: Side walks alternate a stride with arms at the sides (96/32) and a legs-together passing step with both arms swung wide (112/48). Up and down walks alternate which foot is kicked up, the arm on the same side swinging out; the down-walk legs are pixel-identical to the up-walk legs (64=16, 80=0 below the waist). Each arm-out pair goes feet together (160, 128) then a braced stride with the body dropped a pixel (176, 144). Idle A is hands on hips, blinking and tapping the screen-left foot together (192=224 eyes shut and foot up, 208=240 eyes open and foot down). Idle B turns the head screen-left with the arms spread, front with arms hanging, screen-right with arms spread, front again (272=304).
pattern.scuba: 20 frames in the order the engine uses, and this world follows it. Walk frames come in pairs, a wide stride and a closer one; the two up frames and the two down frames swap which foot is lower; the arm-out frames reach with one raised hand. Idle A (12-15) and idle B (16-19) share a front-facing pose with a teal bubble that rises one step per frame, and a blink or foot-tap frame in each.
pattern.player: Twenty frames in six groups, matching the engine order. Frames 0-1 walk LEFT and 4-5 walk RIGHT (a wide stride, then a narrow step, mirrored); 2-3 walk UP seen from behind and 6-7 walk DOWN towards the viewer, each pair swapping which foot is lifted and which side shows the football tip. Frames 8-9 and 10-11 are the arm out LEFT and RIGHT, each pair shifting about a pixel. Frames 12-15 are idle A, a crouch that goes down and back up (12, 13, 14, 13). Frames 16-19 are idle B, a head turn (16 and 19 equal 12, 17 and 18 turned to screen-left). The layout matches the engine facts.
pattern.music: Follows the engine order: frames 0-1 walk left, 2-3 up (back view), 4-5 right, 6-7 down (face view), 8-9 arm out left, 10-11 arm out right, 12-15 idle A and 16-19 idle B. In each walk pair one frame has the feet together as a single shoe block and the other has them apart, and in the up and down pairs the lifted foot and the higher hand swap sides. The idle frames stand still and only change the mouth, the eyes (shut once) and a tipped screen-right shoe, so idle B is mostly a repeat of frames 12 and 13.
pattern.luck: The 20 frames follow the engine layout: frames 0-1 walk LEFT, 2-3 UP (from behind), 4-5 RIGHT, 6-7 DOWN, 8-9 arm out LEFT, 10-11 arm out RIGHT, 12-15 idle A and 16-19 idle B. In the walks the pair alternates a passing step (legs together) and a stride (legs apart), though frames 0 and 5 are the legs-together ones and 1 and 4 the stride; in UP and DOWN the pair swaps which boot is lifted. The arm-out pairs keep the arm fixed and swap legs together and apart. Idle A sinks the head one row lower each frame under the fixed hat, and idle B reuses frames 14, 13, 13 with the eyes shut, then 13 again.
pattern.miner: Frames 0-1, 2-3, 4-5 and 6-7 are the walk cycles for left, up, right and down, each a two-step swap of legs; the right-hand walk mirrors the left, with frame 5 matching frame 0 and frame 4 matching frame 1. Frames 8-11 are the arm-out poses, a bent arm and a stretched arm either side; the idle frames 12-19 keep the same front-facing miner, shift the head by a pixel, blink, then bring the screen-right hand in across the belly.

pattern.hunter: Angles are clockwise from straight up: 0 up, 90 screen-right, 180 down, 270 screen-left. A bat always seen from directly above, head leading. Four headings in index order LEFT (frames 0,1), UP (2,3), RIGHT (4,5), DOWN (6,7) - 270, 0, 90, 180, a clockwise turn in 90-degree steps, exactly the engine's facing. Each heading has two frames: even = wings SPREAD wide at right angles to the body, odd = wings FOLDED back into a narrow dart. So the spread runs vertically in the left/right frames and horizontally in the up/down frames. Frames 4 and 6 are exact pixel mirror/rotation copies of frame 0 (and 5, 7 of 1); the up pair was drawn separately.
pattern.cook: Angles are clockwise from straight up: 0 up, 90 screen-right, 180 down, 270 screen-left. Built like a butterfly: two slices of bread are the wings, a green stalk is the body, and a V-shaped fork at one end (two antenna prongs) is the front. Headings in index order: frames 0,1 UP-LEFT (315), 2,3 UP (0), 4,5 UP-RIGHT (45), 6,7 DOWN (180). The left and right pairs are side views tilted 45 degrees upward, not level. Even frames = wings open (one bread slice as a big diamond in side view; both slices flat either side from above), odd frames = wings closed into a narrow slice.
pattern.cowboy: Angles are clockwise from straight up: 0 up, 90 screen-right, 180 down, 270 screen-left. A plain spin, no wings and no folding. In index order the hammer head points 180, 225, 270, 315, 0, 45, 90, 135 - one full clockwise turn in 45-degree steps. Even frames lie on an axis (handle vertical or horizontal), odd frames on a diagonal, 45 degrees further clockwise. Frames 4, 6 are exact 90 and 180-degree turns of frame 2 (5, 7 of 3). The head does NOT point where the enemy moves: it points 90 degrees anticlockwise of travel (moving left, head down; moving up, head left).
pattern.space: Angles are clockwise from straight up: 0 up, 90 screen-right, 180 down, 270 screen-left. A flame bird, head leading. Headings in index order LEFT (0,1), UP (2,3), RIGHT (4,5), DOWN (6,7), matching the engine's facing. The left and right pairs are SIDE PROFILES: even = one wing raised straight up over the back, odd = wing lowered flat along the back. The up and down pairs are seen from above, head leading: even = both wings spread wide, odd = wings folded narrow. The down pair is the up pair turned upside down.
pattern.body: Angles are clockwise from straight up: 0 up, 90 screen-right, 180 down, 270 screen-left. The same butterfly layout as the cook world: two ears are the wings, the blue probe is the body, and its forked end is the front. Frames 0,1 UP-LEFT (315), 2,3 UP (0), 4,5 UP-RIGHT (45), 6,7 DOWN (180). Left and right pairs are side views tilted 45 degrees upward showing ONE ear; up and down pairs show both ears as a mirrored pair. Even = ear(s) open, odd = closed into a narrow strip.
pattern.scuba: Four facings of the manta-ray creature, each a pair: LEFT lies sideways, UP is upright with a fork at the top, RIGHT mirrors LEFT, DOWN is UP upside down. Within a pair, the wings flex between level (or folded) and swept.
pattern.player: Eight frames in four pairs, in the engine order LEFT, UP, RIGHT, DOWN. In every pair the first frame has the butterfly's wings spread and the second has them folded, so it flaps. LEFT and RIGHT are drawn on a diagonal and mirror each other; UP and DOWN are the same butterfly with its head at the top or the bottom.
pattern.music: The oval tumbles through four orientations - diagonal upper-left to lower-right, upright, the other diagonal, flat - and then repeats them. The second four (frames 4-7) are almost copies of the first four: frame 7 is identical to frame 3, and frames 4, 5 and 6 differ from 0, 1 and 2 only by a pixel shift or a moved black mark.
pattern.luck: Eight frames, two per direction in the order LEFT, UP, RIGHT, DOWN. In every pair the first frame has the wings spread (about half the tile) and the second has them folded (about a third), so each direction flaps. The RIGHT pair is the LEFT pair turned to face the other way; the UP and DOWN pairs use a grey-left white-right wing arrangement.
pattern.miner: Two frames for each of four facings, in the order left, up, right, down. The round pink body is always at the back and the cyan head at the front, so the body is at the right when it faces left, low when it faces up, at the left when it faces right and high when it faces down. The two ticks in each pair only shuffle the legs and feelers.

pattern.hunter: A cartwheel: each frame is the one before turned 90 degrees CLOCKWISE - head up, head screen-right, head down, head screen-left. Frames 1 and 2 are exact pixel rotations of frame 0; frame 3 is redrawn. The spin is clockwise although this is the anticlockwise enemy.
pattern.cook: The egg turns a quarter clockwise each frame, shown only by where the yolk sits: upper-right, lower-right, lower-left, upper-left. The movement is small (the yolk stays near the centre). The white's outline wobbles a little and the black shadow stays at the lower-left.
pattern.cowboy: Exact quarter-turns clockwise, each frame a pixel rotation of the last: the muzzle points 225, 315, 45, 135 (angles clockwise from straight up). Always diagonal.
pattern.space: Turns a quarter clockwise per frame. Because the spiral has two arms, frames 0 and 2 look almost alike and so do 1 and 3, so on screen it flicks between two orientations 90 degrees apart.
pattern.body: Quarter-turns clockwise: upright, cranium to screen-right, upside down, cranium to screen-left. Frame 1 is frame 0 turned exactly 90 degrees and frame 3 is frame 2 turned exactly 90.
pattern.scuba: One mine, two lights that take turns: blue lit in frames 0 and 3, red lit in frames 1 and 2. Frames 1 and 2 are identical, and frames 0 and 3 differ by one pixel.
pattern.player: Four frames of one football in different rotations, each turned a step from the last, so it seems to spin on the spot. The size stays the same; only the position of the black pentagons and the grey shaded panel moves.
pattern.music: Four quarter turns of the same horn: the black tip moves from the top-right (frame 0) to the left edge (frame 1), the bottom-left (frame 2) and the bottom-right (frame 3), and the bell with its brown and white opening swings round the opposite side each time.
pattern.luck: Four frames of one ball rolling: the white highlight goes from the top, to the left, to the bottom, to the right, and the dark shadow stays on the opposite side to it. The pits stay in the same count while they move round with the ball.
pattern.miner: Four frames of one whirlpool disc, always the same size, with the spiral arms turned round a little each step, so it reads as spinning on the spot. The balance of colour shifts from blue and white to green across the four.

pattern.hunter: The same brown mass boiling: each frame is redrawn with the pattern jittered by one or two pixels (60-75 per cent of pixels match between frames). No outline, no movement across the tile.
pattern.cook: A pulsing cell lattice: the central cell goes small ring, then splits into two, then becomes one large ring, then a medium ring. The pixel layout is identical to space and body, only recoloured.
pattern.cowboy: The same violet mass boiling: each frame is redrawn with the mottle jittered by about a pixel, with the navy arrow-shaped band at mid-left in every frame.
pattern.space: A pulsing cell lattice: the central cell goes small ring, then splits into two, then becomes one large ring, then a medium ring. The pixel layout is identical to cook and body, only recoloured.
pattern.body: A pulsing cell lattice: the central cell goes small ring, then splits into two, then becomes one large ring, then a medium ring. The pixel layout is identical to cook and space, only recoloured.
pattern.scuba: Four frames of the same symmetric pattern, redrawn so the cyan blocks move and resize (corner blocks, then a centre block growing to a large square), as a wobbling bubble texture. Transparent holes move too.
pattern.player: Four frames of the same black ground with salmon pixels and teal-and-grey clusters, every frame scattered differently. Frame 0 has a small ring, frame 2 a large ring, frames 1 and 3 have none.
pattern.music: Not a solid fill. Each frame is the same deep blue field with different sparkles: the plus-shaped stars and dots change position and number (3, 5, 5 and 1 stars), and a small block of magenta or dark red drifts. Frame 3 is the sparest.
pattern.luck: Four frames of the same marbled brown and yellow pattern; only the black plus-shaped hole moves. A big diamond at the upper right (0), small ones at both upper right and lower left (1), a big diamond at the lower left with one pixel left at the upper right (2), a small one at the lower left only (3). The mark shrinks in one place as it grows in another, so it appears to hop across the tile.
pattern.miner: The pattern is a busy yellow and red lattice. A centre motif grows from a small ring (frame 0) to a larger one (1) to the largest octagon (2), then shrinks back (3), so it pulses.

pattern.hunter: No cracks in any frame. The shell is four vertical colour bands; the core swells from a small blob to an oval to filling the egg, then shrinks back to the oval, while its small plus sign moves: left of centre, upper-right, lower-right, upper-left. Frame 3 is frame 1 with the plus on the other side.

Frame 3 falls back to nearly the same as frame 1. So it is a pulse rather than a steady fill.
pattern.music: A four-step countdown on one round disc: the dark red core is a small square in frame 0, absent in frame 1 (grey caps instead), almost the whole disc in frame 2 and a large ragged core in frame 3, while the small brown plus jumps to a different spot in every frame.
pattern.luck: Four frames of a casino chip with a black spade. The spade grows from a tiny blob (0) to a full spade (1), the chip flashes pink with the biggest spade (2), then falls back to the dark red chip with a ringed spade (3).
pattern.miner: Four frames of one pointed grey diamond with red caps, counting down: the white vein is longest in frame 0 and shrinks each frame until only a short bar is left in frame 3. The shape and size do not change.

pattern.hunter: Heads alternate jaws shut and jaws open in every facing; tails swing the tip; the side-on body segment rises and steps its leg, the top-down one swaps which diagonal pair of legs sticks out. Right is the exact mirror of left and down the exact vertical flip of up, but the phases cross: 96 mirrors 48 and 112 mirrors 32.
pattern.cook: Nothing animates: every frame pair is pixel-identical, heads, bodies and tails alike. Each facing only turns the slice so the point leads (head) or trails (tail), with the crust towards the neighbouring segment.
pattern.cowboy: Side-on frames turn the wheels and reshape the smoke; the up and down frames flash the round lamp - dark with a small cross, then lit solid pale - while the rail pixels shift. The wagons turn their spokes side-on and sway sideways when travelling up or down. Right is the exact mirror of left.
pattern.space: No animation: every frame pair is pixel-identical. The fighter, hull cog and tail bracket only rotate with facing, and the thin spar or stub always points at the neighbouring segment.
pattern.body: The hand alternates open and reaching (frame A) with clenched into a claw (frame B) in every facing; the foot rotates so the shin always points at the body and only its toes flex; the ribcage turns its spine along the direction of travel and does not animate. No mirroring: each facing is redrawn.
pattern.scuba: A black lamprey-like worm. Heads have four facings with the salmon sucker-mouth at the leading end; the odd frame of each pair has a larger mouth (a pulse). Tails are black wedges with a cyan streak that taper away from the direction of travel. Bodies are black ovals, two vertical and two horizontal, with a cyan glint and dark red veins.
pattern.player: Heads (8), tails (8) and body (4). Each facing has a pair of frames; in the heads the pair differs by a one-row bob, in the tails by the tail's angle. Heads facing UP and RIGHT match that order but the head for DOWN frame 1 (80,96) is drawn left-facing, so the engine's DOWN pair does not look like a front view in both frames. The body pairs are exact duplicates.
pattern.music: Heads: each facing has two frames that are nearly the same drawing (the cyan ring with black outline, whiskers trailing behind), differing only by a few pixels of glints and whisker tips, so it shimmers rather than moves. Facing changes by rotating or flipping the ring: UP and DOWN are mirror images top to bottom, LEFT and RIGHT are mirrors left to right. Body: two vertical and two horizontal frames of the cyan star. Tail: thin magenta strands that run the same way as the facing, with a small glint that moves between the two frames of each direction.
pattern.luck: Heads LEFT, UP, RIGHT, DOWN (two frames each), then bodies (horizontal pair, vertical pair) then tails LEFT, UP, RIGHT, DOWN. The two frames of each head are identical (LEFT differs by one corner pixel pair), and likewise each body pair, so heads and bodies do not animate. Only the tails move: the card shifts two pixels between the two frames (up and down for LEFT and RIGHT, left and right for UP and DOWN).
pattern.miner: Heads come in pairs for each of four facings: one frame with the jaws wide or split and one with them narrow or shut. The body has two frames whose orange legs slide a step, one horizontal pair and one vertical pair. The tails are curved hooks in pairs, a bowl shape and a flatter bridge shape, and the right-facing tails mirror the left-facing ones.

pattern.hunter: No cracks in any frame. A vertical slit in a banded egg opens like an eye: thin slit, wider slit, a big diamond with one dot at its centre, then it closes to a small square block with no dot.
pattern.cook: No cracks in any frame. A vertical slit in a banded egg opens like an eye: thin slit, wider slit, a big diamond with one dot at its centre, then it closes to a small square block with no dot.

pattern.scuba: The cyan bubble with a magenta kernel that swells: about 4, 6, 9, then back to 6 px across.
pattern.player: Four frames of a countdown: the dark grey centre widens from a narrow stripe (frame 0) to a block (frame 1) and nearly the whole width (frame 2, with a white pixel at the centre), then falls back to a smaller block (frame 3). Red shows less and less until frame 2.
pattern.music: A four-step countdown on one round disc: yellow stays on the left, and the right half goes from magenta (frame 0) to salmon-pink (frames 1-3) while the dark red centre widens from a bar to a band, then a diamond with a black centre pixel, then shrinks to a small square core.
pattern.luck: A countdown on a pink, purple and blue bead holding a dark red heart. A black stripe through the middle widens to a black diamond (frames 0 to 2), then is replaced by bright magenta patches (3) as the heart swells back.
pattern.miner: Four frames of one round striped orb, with its white core stripe thickening from a thin line in frame 0 to a big diamond in frame 2, then shrinking back to a centred block in frame 3. The size of the orb does not change.

pattern.hunter: Side-on heads alternate a toothy grin in profile with the head lifted and teeth hidden; top-down heads sway, leaning one way then the other. Tails flick down then up, and the body's colour boundary ripples. Right is the mirror of left.
pattern.cook: The burger head only blinks - frame B loses the pupils, nothing else moves; it has no legs. The chips re-spread between frames; the body burger is still.
pattern.cowboy: Side-on, the horse alternates legs planted in a stride with airborne, legs tucked; from behind and in front it alternates which leg reaches the ground. The wagons turn their wheels side-on and sway when seen from above.
pattern.space: No animation: every pair is pixel-identical. The saucer, lattice body and tail disc only rotate, the thin spar always pointing at the neighbouring segment.
pattern.body: As the skeleton: the hand alternates open and reaching with clenched into a claw; the foot rotates so the ankle always points at the body and only the toes flex; the flesh body turns its folds with the direction and does not animate.
pattern.scuba: A green sea dragon. Heads: UP and DOWN show two eyes from above, LEFT and RIGHT show one eye in profile, with the dark red mouth at the leading end; the odd frame of each pair opens the mouth wider or shifts the head. Tails are forked fish fins joined to the body end, a larger and a smaller fork per facing. Bodies are round green and cyan segments, vertical and horizontal pairs.
pattern.player: Heads (8), tails (8) and body (4), in the same pose layout as the evil worm. In the heads each pair differs by a one-row bob; the front-view DOWN pair shows the black dome and grey grid in both frames. Tails are the starburst with two streaks, which sweep one way and then the other between the pair. The horizontal body pair differs by two pixels, the vertical pair not at all.
pattern.music: Heads: each facing has two frames that are nearly the same drawing (the salmon-pink treble clef, upright for LEFT and RIGHT, lying on its side for UP and DOWN), differing only by a few glint and staff-line pixels, so it shimmers rather than moves. The dark red staff lines trail behind: below for UP, above for DOWN, left for RIGHT, right for LEFT. Body: two vertical and two horizontal scroll frames. Tail: thin dark red strands in the same directions as the evil worm's, with a small glint that moves between frames.
pattern.luck: Same layout as the evil worm (heads, then bodies, then tails) but with red hearts instead of black spades. Heads barely change between the two frames of a facing. In every body and tail pair the heart changes colour: pink in the first frame, dark red in the second, and for the tails the card also shifts two pixels.
pattern.miner: This worm is a mine train: a steam locomotive for the head, ore wagons for the body and a last ore wagon for the tail. Each facing has two frames that differ only in small details, smoke and wheel spokes for the side-on views, and the red lamp growing from a plus to a disc in the head from above. Left and right are mirrored, and up and down are the wagon seen from above.

pattern.hunter: The four frames are ONE picture scrolling left like a conveyor: each frame is the wall tile moved 4 px to screen-left, wrapping round, so frame 1 is shifted 4 px, frame 2 8 px and frame 3 12 px, and the fourth step lands back on frame 0. Nothing changes but the horizontal position: no colour change, no new motif, no vertical movement.

pattern.scuba: Four independent random-looking arrangements of the same stony colours; they differ in about 215 of 256 pixels, so the wall appears to shimmer rather than change shape.
pattern.player: Frame 0 is the colourful wall (shared with the wall tile); frames 1-3 are the same stone with the coloured inlay removed and the pattern shifted sideways a few pixels each time.
pattern.music: The piano keyboard slid sideways 2 px per frame across the four frames (black keys start at col 1, 7, 5 and 3 in the order plain wall, 164, 196, 228). It is the same drawing shifted, not a different picture.
pattern.luck: Four frames of the brown link wall. The gleam pixel in each window runs yellow, bright green, dark green, bright green. The pattern also moves: frame 1 is about four pixels left of frame 0, frame 2 has the two rows swapped from frame 0, and frame 3 has frame 1's pattern with the two rows swapped.
pattern.miner: The same rock and vein texture in all four frames, moved down by 4 rows each frame with wrap-round. This is exact, pixel for pixel, so the vein seems to run downwards.

pattern.hunter: A single still tile: the same sprite (132,4) as the plain wall. It does not animate and it has nothing of its own.

pattern.cook: The tap itself never changes; only the cross handle on top turns, drawn wide, narrower, end-on, then widening again (about 10, 8, 4, 6 px) - a continuous spin. No liquid is drawn leaving the spout.

pattern.player: Four frames sharing an identical lower body. Only the crossbar at the top changes, 10, 8, 4 then 6 px wide.
pattern.music: The pipework is the same in every frame except frame 0 (an extra thin vertical line at col 1). The only real change between frames is the specks of drip at the top, which move and regroup each frame.

pattern.miner: A blue drop falls (frames 0 and 1, the second fatter and lower), breaks into a puddle and flying fragments (2 and 3), and settles as a round glossy ball (4 and 5, the second fuller).

pattern.cook: The clockwise enemy turning into the treasure: the split shape gains a red rim, its seam widens, the halves join into one slice, then a whole apple slice with a stalk.
pattern.cowboy: The clockwise enemy turning into the treasure: the hammer tilted and coming apart, an all-over scatter of multicoloured specks, the specks gathering into the left of a disc, then the whole jewelled coin.

pattern.body: The clockwise enemy turning into the treasure: the ear with red appearing inside, red filling it, a red heart with a gem, then the finished heart.
pattern.scuba: Four frames: a magenta ball loses its colour as a grey and white diamond grows from the middle, ending as a full diamond. Frame 3 is grey and white, unlike the coral and yellow treasure.

pattern.music: A burst that grows frame by frame, from about 45% of the tile (frame 0) to about 70% (frame 3). The black tip at the top left is the same in each, and the coral and yellow mass thickens and spreads to the right.

pattern.miner: A spray of cyan sparks and a small white and magenta lump (frames 0 and 1) builds up into a larger lump (2) and then almost the full gem (3).

animations.object: Boulder to anticlockwise enemy, and back

pattern.hunter: Not a morph with both shapes side by side: the monkey dissolves into a scatter of loose pixels over the whole tile, and the rock condenses out of the scatter. Only the two end frames show a recognisable object.
pattern.cook: A smooth growth in place: the yolk swells until it is the orange, while the egg white shrinks to a thin rim and goes.
pattern.cowboy: A pixel dissolve: the revolver's grey breaks up into a speckled cloud and green-brown cactus speckle takes over. The middle two frames show no clear object.
pattern.space: The galaxy never appears in this chain: the first frame is already a round globe, just filled with galaxy blues. Green land fades in patch by patch.
pattern.body: The eye opens out of the skull's face: first a blue dot at the nose, then a white with an iris spreading across the face until the skull is gone.
pattern.scuba: Four steps from nearly all grey mine (0x34) to nearly all aqua shell (0x37), running either way. The shell grows in from the right and bottom, and the mine shrinks to the left and top.
pattern.player: Four frames running from the football (240,160) to the black boulder (192,160). The football panels break up and fade into black, and the boulder's grey and white highlight appears at the right. Black rises from about 45% to 61% of the tile.
pattern.music: Four steps in one picture that breaks up: from a roughly round dark grey and brown mottled mass (192,160), through a looser mix of grey and brown (208), to scattered brown, grey and dark red flecks (224), to a thin scatter of brown and dark red (240). The grey drains out and the dark red specks increase as the frames go from 192 to 240.
pattern.luck: Four frames listed from the pale grey enemy ball (240,160) back to the black billiard ball (192,160). Pale grey with black pits spreads up from the bottom as the black ball and its white 8 disc recede; read the other way it is the boulder turning grey.
pattern.miner: The green, blue and white whirlpool disc and the red ore lump swap places over four frames. Frame 0 is almost all spiral and frame 3 almost all lump, with blue and green fragments left at the left side in between.

pattern.hunter: The rock scatters into loose fragments and the gold gathers out of them. No frame shows both whole objects side by side, and no frame shows a face until the last.
pattern.cook: The orange changes in place: red skin creeps round its edge, cream flesh opens up, and a green gem grows from a two-pixel dot at the centre.
pattern.cowboy: A pixel dissolve: green-brown speckle gives way to gold, red and blue speckle; the coin only takes shape in the last frame.
pattern.space: The Earth shrinks towards the centre while a ring of rays grows round it, until the Earth is only the sun's core.
pattern.body: The eye stays centred while a heart-shaped red rim grows round it and the pupil turns into the green gem. The heart is a symbol heart (two lobes and a point), not an anatomical one.
pattern.scuba: Four steps from mostly shell (0x17) to almost all red and yellow gem (0x1A). The gem grows downwards from the top right corner; the shell is left as a band along the bottom.
pattern.player: Four frames running from the black ball with only cup corners showing (240,176) to the nearly complete trophy (192,176). Black falls from about 49% to 4% as the yellow bowl, stem and base fill in and the ball shrinks to a small patch in the bowl.
pattern.music: Four steps in one picture: a light grey mass with a black edge and a few coloured flecks (240,176) is slowly wrapped by a yellow and pink flame (224, 208) until the flame dominates and the grey shrinks to a core (192,176).
pattern.luck: Four frames listed from the black billiard ball (240,176) to the green four-leaf clover (192,176). The black ball with its white 8 disc recedes and the clover's leaves grow out from behind it, edges first; read the other way it is the treasure being swallowed by the boulder.
pattern.miner: The red ore lump gives way to a white, pink and blue gem burst over four frames. The pink and white star in the centre grows in each frame while the red lump shrinks to a ragged edge.

scuba: Every scuba sprite is drawn on a solid royal-blue sea ground (0,0,170), not on transparency, so the 'background' in each tile is blue. Only a few tiles (growth, wall-b, bonus-turn, lamp, flame, the first good-worm head) have transparent pixels, and in the lamp they are interior holes.
The exit does not hinge like the 1988 doors: the closed hatch (192,112) parts into an upper and a lower half that move apart vertically, revealing a brown ladder in a black opening.

The treasure (256,128) is a salmon-red and yellow gem, but the treasure blast (256..304,144) ends on a grey and white diamond, so the two do not match; the to-treasure transformation does end on the red and yellow gem.

Walls (wall-1 to wall-4, special-wall, wall-b) are busy mosaics of colour fragments; no single object can be identified in them. The four numbered walls are all the same kind of mosaic, each a different arrangement.

enemy-a read as a manta ray, enemy-b as a spiked sea mine, wormA as a lamprey-like black creature and wormB as a green sea dragon: the identifications are judgements from shapes and colours, the pixel descriptions are exact.
Player layout follows the engine facts exactly (walk L/U/R/D, arm out L/R, two idle sets). The idle sets differ from the 1988 style: bubble rises and a blink, no real motion.
Frame 0 and 3 of the anticlockwise enemy differ by one pixel; frames 1 and 2 are identical.
The tile layouts match the facts for the positions I was given.
Treasure (coral and yellow diamond) differs from the last blast-to-treasure frame (grey and white diamond).
The wall, steel, dirt, pass-through wall and timed wall tiles are noise textures with no figurative content; amoeba and pass-through wall have transparent holes.
The time bonus hand and clock gaps are transparent pixels, not drawn grey.
Fire tap is a long-necked bird, not a tap; acid tap is a red water tap.
player: Player layout matches the engine facts for all 20 frames. Idle A (12-15) goes 12, 13, 14, 13 (a crouch down and back), and idle B (16-19) has 16 = 19 = 12 exactly, with 17 = 18 turned.
The tile background is opaque green (0,170,0), not transparent, so the 'solid' versus 'free' check of a tile has to ignore it.

Evil worm head (80,96) is drawn left-facing (glint upper left, notch and legs lower left), though the engine uses it as the DOWN frame 1. The good worm's (80,80) is a front view like (64,80). The evil heads (96,96) and (112,96) are also left-facing but the glint is upper left in (80,96) and (96,96) and upper right in (112,96).
In the evil worm the glint is on the upper left in LEFT frames 80 and 96 but in the good worm it is always upper right.
The player boy is a football player (red helmet, grey face guard, brown football). Not all palette letters are the same between frames; descriptions use the actual colours.
Wall-1 differs from wall-2 to wall-4: it has yellow outlines and a dark blue and a red cross shape; the other three are near-identical.
Drip, lamp, tap and flame read as dark red, black and grey objects. I could not identify what they are meant to be, so the subjects describe the colours and shapes only.
Worm head 'legs' and 'cage' readings are by pixels. The grey shapes under the heads could be legs, bars or a face guard; I describe them as legs and a grey grid.
Treasure-blast frame 256,144 is a yellow and red butterfly shape with a black T-shaped stem, that dissolves to a trophy at 304,144. Only the subject line is mine.
Treasure bonus frame 1 (16,128) has one stray teal pixel at the left edge (col 0, row 8) that is in no other frame.
The timed wall frame 0 (132,4) is a decorated stone wall, while frames 1-3 (164,4 / 196,4 / 228,4) are plain stone, so the gems vanish after frame 0.
Acid tap and fire tap are drawn as black angular shapes with salmon highlights; I could not tell what object they depict, so the readings describe only shapes.
The two taps animate different parts: the acid tap's top, the fire tap's foot.
Fire (128..176,112) has no flame colours: it is grey and black only.
Time bonus hand: it is a thick bar with a lower-right stub that does not rotate, so it is not a true rotation, just the bar moving to four positions.
Boulder is one 1988-grid tile at (0,64) with transparent-free green corners; no placeholder.
fire tap has two transparent pixels at col 10 rows 0-1 in each frame.
music: enemy-a is not identified: a salmon-pink oval with brown shading, yellow and white glints and a small black and dark red mark; described by appearance only.
enemy-b reads as a yellow brass horn (bell with a brown and white opening, long tube to a black tip) but this is an interpretation from shape, not certain.
evil worm head (cyan ring with prongs and whiskers) and body (cyan X star) are not clearly any one instrument; described by shape only.
good worm head and body look like a treble clef with dark red staff lines; tails are staff-line strands.

Rockford layout follows the engine facts: frames 0-1 left, 2-3 up from behind, 4-5 right, 6-7 down, 8-9 arm left, 10-11 arm right, 12-19 idle. In frames 0 and 5 and 10 the feet are one wide block, in 1, 4, 11 two shoes apart, which is the opposite of the example hunter reading.
Idle frames 12, 16 and 18 are identical, and 17 and 19 are identical; 13 is 17 plus an open mouth.
Frames 6 and 7 sit one row higher than the idle poses (bottom row empty).
to-boulder tiles (192-240,160) do not look like the black record boulder: they are dark grey and brown mottle with see-through gaps and dark red specks.
Tail tiles (128-240,96 and 80) have identical geometry for evil and good worm; only colour differs (magenta vs dark red; evil 128 has green, evil 240 has dark red bits).
Several tiles contain transparent pixels (lamp 256,64, the to-boulder frames); the grids mark them as blank.
Amoeba tile is a sparse starfield on deep blue, not a solid tile.
Fire tap, fire and the clock hand use see-through pixels, so their drawn colours depend on what is behind them.
Pass-through wall and treasure are hard to name by pixels; the descriptions say what is drawn, not what it is.
Boulder is a black vinyl record, not a rock.
luck: Luck is a card and casino theme: the player is a gambler in a red hat, the worms are playing cards (evil = black spades, good = red hearts), eggs are casino-chip-like, the boulder is a black billiard ball.

The layout matches the engine facts for the player, enemies, worms and eggs, with one point: in the walk pairs the legs-together frames are 0, 5, 8 and 11 and the stride frames are 1, 4, 9 and 10, which is the reverse of the order the hunter example uses. In UP and DOWN walking the pair swaps the lifted boot.

Evil worm heads and bodies do not animate: each pair of frames is identical (LEFT head differs by one corner pixel pair). Good worm heads are the same apart from DOWN, where frame b is the figure shifted about a pixel. Only the tails shift position, and good worms flip pink to dark red per frame.

wall-b is a rounded brown shape with dark grey streaks on yellow that I could not identify with confidence; the wall-1 to wall-4 tiles look like scrolled slices of one picture (brown and grey panels around black windows with a dot) and I did not name the subject.
The lamp (fire tap) is a flame-coloured bird-like figure rather than a tap; its upper body stays still and the crest and foot flicker.
The player carries a short light grey bar at his left side (screen-left in front and back views) that I could not identify; I called it a pistol or blade.

The head figure on the worm cards is jagged and I could only describe it as joker-like. The evil head's black mass leads in the facing direction in all four views, which agrees with the engine layout.
Transparent pixels are see-through in the sheet. The enemy ball pits and the exit window and open doorway are transparent, not black.

Positions with y=4 or y=28 (steel 68,4; the walls 132..228,4; pass-through 68,28) are the 16x16 crops of 3D box icons in a sheet that is not on the 16-pixel grid, so the crop is not a clean tile: steel straddles a red face with a heart and a black face with a cyan diamond; the wall icons show a pair of windows twice. I described exactly what each crop shows.
The expanding wall and the plain wall share 132,4 with the timed wall's frame 0, so there is one reading for it.

The treasure bonus uses the four card suits in order (heart, diamond, spade, club) in place of the numbers 0 to 3; the time bonus is a clock whose hand turns a quarter each frame, up, right, down, left.
The clover in the treasure tile and the last blast-to-treasure frame differ by two pixels only.
Fire tap and acid tap: the shape is a spout or pipe, not obviously a tap; the animating part is the top cap on the acid tap and the bottom stem on the fire tap.
Exit frame 0 has a spade-shaped hole in the door slab, and the hole is transparent.
Dirt, steel, wall, pass-through and boulder have no multiple frames.
miner: Player frame order matches the engine facts exactly: 0,1 left; 2,3 up from behind; 4,5 right; 6,7 down; 8,9 arm out left; 10,11 arm out right; 12-19 idle. Idle A is two pairs of identical frames, so 12=13 and 14=15=16.
The miner's red face and the red and orange evil worm are drawn in unusual colours; descriptions follow the pixels. The brown strip beside the face is hair.
Evil worm is not a train: it looks like a red and orange centipede with curved jaws, orange legs and a hooked tail. This is an identification from shape, not stated by the sheet.
Good worm is a mine train: steam locomotive head, ore wagon body and tail. Its up and down heads show a red lamp or smoke puff, ambiguous from above.
Fire tap (role lamp) looks like a bird at first sight: a jagged crest on an upright stem, a pipe arm to the left and a foot. I described it as a burner built like an upside-down tap.
Boulder to treasure: the final frame 0x1A is a starburst, not the finished gem.
Transparent pixels show as black in the game, so 'black gaps' in the readings are empty (transparent) pixels.
The tile at 132,4 is shared by the wall, the expanding wall and frame 0 of the timed wall, so it has one reading.
The fire tap (256..304,64) is drawn as a standing bird in light red, dark red and yellow, not a tap. Only its feet animate.
The acid tap (256..304,176) is drawn as an actual tap but in red, orange and yellow (a molten look), not blue. The falling acid (0..80,112) is blue. The fire (128..176,112) is a red flame.
The boulder tile (0,64) is lopsided and ragged, shifted to the right of the tile, and is not an obviously recognisable object.
Dirt, steel and pass-through wall are not full-bleed: about a third of their pixels are transparent gaps.
Wall is a left half of red and yellow vein against a right half of grey rock, not an evenly tiled texture.
Time bonus: the dark red hand has a fixed short diagonal tail towards the lower right in all frames, which I took to be part of the hand drawing.
Amoeba centre-motif sizes (2x2, 3x3, 6x6, about 4x3 px of yellow) were measured from the nearest yellow region to the tile centre.
